I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize system, because that matches my fields, my irrigation conditions, and what I know best after 40 years. I have only 7.7 mu, so I will not spread myself too thin. I will put 6.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 1.7 mu in cotton. Because I am experienced and educated, I prefer improved or hybrid seed where it clearly raises stability and yield. I also have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key stages rather than farm as if I were fully rainfed. At my age, I will also choose operations that save labor and reduce repeated field work, so I will use rotary tillage for wheat and cotton, and no-tillage summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and moisture. I will fertilize steadily rather than aggressively, aiming for reliable output instead of chasing maximum yield. For cotton, I will manage more carefully for insects because it is the crop on my farm that usually demands the most attention. For wheat and maize, I will keep inputs moderate and timely, because on my scale, timing matters more than pushing every input to the maximum.
